label: D2 after a2 led rarely to S1 (a2 -> S1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S1 (the rare transition for a2): 99.7% of activation mass falls in this case. It is silent at D1 and GO, after a1 choices (including a1->S2 rare, so it is specific to the a2->S1 transition, not rare transitions in general), and after common transitions. Recall is 0.97. Precision (0.75) is lost mostly late in the episode: the feature fades after about trial 70 and is silent in trials 90-99. Adding ep_trial < 85 raises dev F1 from 0.845 to 0.916, but the simpler predicate was recorded. Magnitude is higher when the rare S1 outcome follows an earlier reward or another recent rare transition, as in the top windows (e.g. r1 at that D1 or repeated a2->S1). The weakest activations are isolated a2->S1 events after a run of common rewarded trials. Every variable used is observed at D2.

issues: The core claims hold on test. Predicate (phase==D2)&(action==2)&(state==1) gives P 0.733, R 0.972, F1 0.836, mass recall 0.996. Mass recall is 0.000 for phase==GO, 0.000 for phase==D1, 0.000 for D2 a1->S2 rare, and 0.0004 for D2 common transitions. So the feature fires at D2 only, on a2->S1 only, and not on rare transitions in general.

There is a systematic false-positive class in the recorded predicate: late-episode trials. Test precision within the predicate by ep_trial: <20: 0.93, 20-50: 0.94, 50-70: 0.87, 70-80: 0.73, 80-90: 0.32, >=90: 0.00 (6036 predicted steps, none active). The trials with ep_trial>=85 make up 9285 of 57153 predicted steps (16%) at precision 0.049. The explanation mentions this but the predicate and label leave it out, so most of the precision loss is a known, structured gap and not noise.

Adding ep_trial<85 brings test P from 0.733 to 0.866 with almost no loss (R 0.961, mass recall 0.995), and test F1 from 0.836 to 0.911. The false positives that remain (6430 steps) look scattered across reward, transition and context patterns, with no clear structure.

Some magnitude variation is left unexplained. Activation is higher when good==S2 (mass 0.73) than when good==S1 (0.17), and higher with prev_reward==1 (0.76) than with prev_reward==0 (0.23). This is graded modulation, not a gating condition, so it does not refute the label.
No future variables are needed. Every variable used (phase, action, state, ep_trial) is observed at D2.
